claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children under 16 years old, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training that you're responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking into claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 20 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I appreciate you providing that context.

Since Alex is 20 years old, I need to ask you a few clarifying questions to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, as the rules are different for children aged 16 and over.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (for example, at university, college, or a training programme)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, I'm not able to confirm your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you'll usually still qualify if they're under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in approved education or training, he would not qualify for Child Benefit under the standard rules.

However, before I make a final determination, let me ask one more question:

**Is there any possibility that Alex might be registering with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, or has he recently left education or training?** This could potentially allow for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks in certain circumstances.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces, and he didn't recently leave education either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided, I can now provide you with a clear outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The reason is that Alex is 20 years old and is not in approved education or training. Child Benefit is normally paid for children under 16, and can continue for those aged 16-19 only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex exceeds both of these criteria, he does not qualify.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he enters approved education or training before reaching age 20 - you may be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that point. I'd recommend contacting HMRC (HM Revenue and Customs) if you have any further questions or if his situation changes.
